expectations.text: Explains that FedRAMP baselines derive from FIPS 199 impact categorization: Low = limited adverse effect, Moderate = serious adverse effect, High = severe or catastrophic adverse effect
expectations.evidence: "Low / Class B: ... a breach would cause limited harm"; "Moderate / Class C: ... A breach would cause serious adverse effects"; "High / Class D: ... compromise would have a severe or catastrophic effect."

expectations.text: States or implies the correct baseline rigor progression (approx. 156 controls Low, 323 Moderate, 421 High under NIST 800-53 Rev 5, or an equivalent statement that control count and assessment rigor increase with level)
expectations.evidence: "Roughly 156 controls under NIST 800-53 Rev 5" (Low); "323 controls" (Moderate); "421 controls — the most demanding baseline" (High) — exact match to ground-truth figures.

expectations.text: Identifies that law-enforcement-sensitive data typically maps to FedRAMP High (the High baseline was designed for law enforcement, emergency services, financial and health systems) or at minimum Moderate-to-High with a reasoned FIPS 199 analysis
expectations.evidence: "you should plan for the High baseline — Certification Class D ... Class D is for 'federal information where compromise has severe or catastrophic effect (e.g., law enforcement, financial, health data)'" with supporting FIPS 199 reasoning.

expectations.text: If the answer mentions CR26 Certification Classes, the mapping matches official FedRAMP notice NTC-0004: Class A = new pilot/transitional baseline, Class B = LI-SaaS + Low, Class C = Moderate, Class D = High. FAIL if it presents an incorrect mapping. PASS if classes are not mentioned at all.
expectations.evidence: Mapping table: LI-SaaS+Low -> Class B, Moderate -> Class C, High -> Class D, Class A = 'new pilot/transitional tier, entry via external frameworks.' Matches NTC-0004 exactly.

expectations.text: Notes that the final security categorization / risk acceptance decision rests with the authorizing agency (per RMF and NTC-0004: a FedRAMP certification is not itself an agency risk acceptance)
expectations.evidence: "This determination isn't self-certifying ... always confirm with your sponsoring agency before finalizing" and closing note: "The final impact-level determination should be validated with your sponsoring federal agency."
